name: David Ben-Gurion
role: First Prime Minister of Israel (1886-1973), Labour Zionist leader
summary: Ben-Gurion, Labour Zionist leader and Israel's first Prime Minister, proclaimed the Jewish state in 1948 with equal rights for all inhabitants and an open door for Jewish immigration, and defended Israel's security against Egypt and the United Nations in 1956-57.

sources.title: Declaration of Israel's Independence, Tel Aviv, 14 May 1948 (read and proclaimed by Ben-Gurion), Avalon Project, Yale Law School
sources.author: David Ben-Gurion and the People's Council
sources.usedFor: His proclamation of the State of Israel on 14 May 1948 (he read the Declaration): a Jewish state, the right of return, self-determination, freedom of religion.

sources.title: Speech to the United Nations Demanding Security Guarantees, 23 January 1957, Jewish Virtual Library
sources.author: David Ben-Gurion
sources.usedFor: Free navigation, Egypt, the UN Emergency Force and Israel's security.

sources.title: Speech to the Knesset on the Situation in Sinai, February 1957, Jewish Virtual Library
sources.author: David Ben-Gurion
sources.usedFor: The dispute with the United Nations and the United States over withdrawal and double standards.

sources.title: David Ben-Gurion, Wikipedia
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Background only; no answer rests on it.

sources.title: Knesset protocol, 15 October 1956 (Third Knesset): Prime Minister's statement on foreign policy and security (Hebrew PDF, fs.knesset.gov.il)
sources.author: David Ben-Gurion
sources.usedFor: His Knesset statement of 15 Oct 1956: doubts on the UN's ability to act, security, arms purchases.

sources.title: Knesset protocol, 6 March 1956 (Third Knesset, 92nd sitting): question time, Defence Minister Ben-Gurion's answers on administrative detention under the military government (Hebrew PDF, fs.knesset.gov.il)
sources.author: David Ben-Gurion
sources.usedFor: As Defence Minister he defended administrative detention orders by military governors against Arab villagers and refused an MK's challenge.

sources.title: The 'Status Quo' letter of 19 June 1947 to Agudat Israel, text printed in Hamodia, 9 January 2014 ('The History of the Status Quo Agreement')
sources.author: D. Ben-Gurion, Rabbi J. L. Fishman, Y. Gruenbaum, for the Jewish Agency Executive
sources.usedFor: The commitments he signed for the Jewish Agency: Shabbat as the legal day of rest, kosher food in government kitchens, autonomy for each religious educational stream.

sources.title: Israel's Basic Laws: The Law of Return (5 July 1950), Jewish Virtual Library
sources.author: Knesset (bill presented by Prime Minister Ben-Gurion)
sources.usedFor: Text of the 1950 law he introduced: every Jew has the right to come to Israel as an oleh.

sources.title: Law of Return, Encyclopaedia Judaica (via encyclopedia.com)
sources.author: Encyclopaedia Judaica
sources.usedFor: Quotes his speech presenting the bill (the right 'preceded the State of Israel') and explains the law.

sources.title: The 'People's Army'? Ultra-Orthodox conscription and the yeshiva deferment, Israel Democracy Institute
sources.author: Israel Democracy Institute
sources.usedFor: His 1948 agreement deferring about 400 yeshiva students and his later doubts.

sources.title: Yeshiva students' draft exemption: timeline (1948-2002), Israel Democracy Institute
sources.author: Israel Democracy Institute
sources.usedFor: Timeline: 1948 approval of the exemption, 1949 Defense Service Law and his use of section 12.

sources.title: How Ben-Gurion's pragmatic decision led to haredim draft exemption - analysis, The Jerusalem Post, 26 June 2024
sources.author: Eli Ashkenazi
sources.usedFor: His October 1948 report to the Provisional State Council, the 1949 extension and Knesset questions.

sources.title: Education in Israel: laws (State Education Law, 1953), Jewish Virtual Library
sources.author: Jewish Virtual Library
sources.usedFor: The 1953 law ending party-affiliated schools and setting 'State education' and 'State-religious education'.

sources.title: Emergency Regulations, Encyclopedia of the Modern Middle East and North Africa (via encyclopedia.com)
sources.author: Encyclopedia of the Modern Middle East and North Africa
sources.usedFor: About 90 percent of Israeli Arabs under military administration 1948-1966, governors appointed by the defence minister.

sources.title: The U.S. Discovery of Israel's Secret Nuclear Project (Avner Cohen and William Burr), National Security Archive Electronic Briefing Book 510
sources.author: Avner Cohen, William Burr
sources.usedFor: In 1955 he launched the secret feasibility initiative for a nuclear programme aimed at producing nuclear explosives, and chose concealment in 1960.

sources.title: Sèvres Protocol (1956), Encyclopedia of the Modern Middle East and North Africa (S. Ilan Troen, via encyclopedia.com)
sources.author: S. Ilan Troen
sources.usedFor: The secret Israeli-British-French agreement he signed to attack Egypt across Sinai on 29 October 1956.

notes: First audit; reworked after review. Answers rest on his acts (record over words): the 1948 proclamation (Declaration), the 1950 Law of Return, the 1947 status-quo letter (text from Hamodia), the yeshiva deferment and Defense Service Law (IDI, Jerusalem Post), the 1953 State Education Law (JVL), military government of Arab citizens (Encyclopedia of the Modern Middle East; his March 1956 Knesset answers), the 1955 nuclear initiative (Cohen and Burr) and the 1956 Sèvres Protocol. His words are kept for the UN answer (January 1957 UN speech, February 1957 Knesset speech, 15 October 1956 Knesset statement, read in Hebrew). The 1960 Knesset statement that Dimona was for peaceful purposes (JTA) is not cited: it contradicts the record in Cohen and Burr, who say he chose concealment, so nuclear answers rest on the record and stay at medium. Read but settling no statement: the 1952 reparations agreement (JVL: Knesset 61-50 vote; his own speech not reached), the 1953 State Education Law's centralising effect (the law text names no statement on centralism). Not reached: the 1952 Nationality Law text and his Knesset speeches on the labour economy and Histadrut, so public-ownership and centralism stay null. israeled.org and torchweb.org (status-quo letter), the Forward and palquest.org refused automated access and were not retried; the Hamodia print copy of the letter was used instead.
